title: Program Kit operation exposure and application capabilities
intent: Let application owners publish exact host-neutral operations and optional outcome capabilities so fresh Codex and Claude Code sessions can invoke registered operations directly or follow application-owned guidance, while Program Kit owns only deterministic projection, conformance, lifecycle, and evidence.
scope: Host-neutral operation catalog and exact Console/OpenAPI exposure bindings.
Reserved generated Console structured introspection for the complete catalog or one exact operation.
One provider-neutral dual-era MCP stdio bridge and deterministic operation-to-tool projection.
Explicit project-scoped Codex and Claude Code tool-registration proposals, ownership locks, status, update, and removal.
Optional application-authored consumer outcome capability bundles with exact operation bindings and finite knowledge closure.
Explicit public/anonymous bundle acquisition, content-addressed storage, verification, initialization, refresh, update, status, removal, preflight, reads, and pruning.
Thin provider-native capability projections, one derived flat workspace catalog, and one on-demand discover-capabilities capability.
Program Kit package-only dogfood and provider-neutral, provider-configuration, genuine-provider, and governance acceptance.
nonGoals: Runtime, CLI, schema, package, host, MCP, provider, capability, lock, catalog, or acceptance implementation under design authority.
Application operation, workflow, result, diagnostic, trigger, intake, remediation, stop, or completion semantics authored or approved by Program Kit.
One capability per command, a universal application result, availableActions, next-action envelope, workflow state machine, or Program Kit confidence router.
Automatic registration, capability initialization, provider start, trust, permission, invocation, retry, handoff, nested tool call, or autonomous model/tool loop.

Remote MCP, MCP Apps or optional extensions, HTTP invocation adapter implementation, private/authenticated bundle acquisition, package-feed publication, release, deployment, infrastructure, production data, secrets, or external repository changes.
assumptions: Application owners can assert exact semantic equivalence when multiple host bindings represent one operation revision.
Open Console and OpenAPI remain independently versioned exposure contracts while binding one operation catalog.
Codex and Claude Code continue to support project-scoped local stdio MCP and provider-native project skills under the cited current official contracts; every affected work unit rechecks them.
Program Kit package distribution can carry inert capability content beside runtime packages without runtime references to agent-session content.
The existing private Program Kit C# gate remains compatible with Program Kit-owned implementation source.
Genuine Claude Code acceptance can be run by the human from the exact reviewed artifacts and returned as provider-labelled evidence.

artifactDecisions.requestedOutcome: Represent host-neutral operations, generated host introspection, dual-era MCP, explicit tool registration, optional application outcome capabilities, exact knowledge closure, deterministic workspace lifecycle, provider-native guidance, and package-only dogfood as one validated review candidate.

executableBehavior.rationale: The design performs and authorizes no implementation, acquisition, registration, capability initialization, provider start, permission, invocation, or acceptance execution.

valueLifecycle.rationale: Canonical bytes are schema/semantic validated, bound by the plan and review manifest, and rechecked before exact approval.

agentRetrieval.rationale: The review artifact is explicit repository input; it does not create or activate a capability.

agentProcedure.rationale: The design describes prospective product capabilities but is not itself an executable provider procedure.

humanCommunication.audience: The human Program Kit reviewer, later bounded implementer, application publishers, provider acceptance operators, and conformance reviewers.
humanCommunication.decisionAuthorityBoundary: Only separate explicit human approval of the exact canonical design and implementation-plan digests authorizes bounded implementation.
humanCommunication.rationale: Canonical JSON, human projections, provider evidence, compatibility, fixtures, validation, and manifest expose the complete decision and proof boundary.

generatedNavigation.rationale: The review README is sufficient navigation.

governance.provenancePolicy: Exact human intent and convergence are bound to committed Program Kit main f555745e77ebce234f7e54665869a32cc555ba45; completed health-patching and package-only consumer work is reconciled but not modified.
governance.digestPolicy: Any byte change requires revalidation, new digests, and renewed exact approval.
governance.compatibilityPolicy: Operation, exposure, introspection, MCP, package, bundle, procedure, closure, provider, lock, catalog, proposal, and evidence identities/version/digests are explicit.
governance.migrationPolicy: Tool registration and capability initialization update independently; refresh reconstructs only same-source derived bytes; incompatible change requires reviewed migration or exact removal/fresh transition.

dataHandling.redactionPolicy: Artifacts contain public identities, versions, digests, relative paths, normalized configuration shapes, and expected outcomes only; secret values, invocation inputs/results, provider credentials, and environment values are excluded.
dataHandling.externalizationPolicy: Canonical operation/capability semantics remain application-owned; Program Kit contracts and conformance remain Program Kit-owned; provider files are exact separately locked projections.
dataHandling.ephemeralDataPolicy: Provider sessions, process state, selection, prompts, permissions, invocation values, and transient proposal previews are evidence observations, not durable design content.

artifactDecisions.rationale: One schema-governed design preserves the semantic, transport, guidance, conformance, lifecycle, provider, and human-authority boundaries without implementing them.

security.policy: Deny undeclared filesystem, network, secret, and authority access; verify every exact catalog, package, executable, schema, bundle, resource, adapter, lock, and projection byte before use.
guarantees: Exact resource and side-effect declarations gate operation projection and invocation.
Knowledge closure contains no undeclared source or network dependency.
Tamper, collision, incompatibility, path escape, missing closure, and unowned state fail before execution or mutation.
exclusions: No secret values, source recovery, configuration adoption, permission grant, sandbox escape, or semantic inference.

authority.policy: Acquisition, tool registration, capability initialization, refresh/update, provider trust/permission, provider-native selection, handoff, and invocation are separate transitions.
guarantees: Every Program Kit mutation previews and requires one exact accepted proposal digest.
Provider/human trust and permission remain inaccessible Program Kit state.
Capability activation and handoff grant no execution authority.
exclusions: No installation activation, self-registration, self-initialization, permission mutation, provider start, automatic handoff, or autonomous loop.

secrets.policy: Secrets are denied by default and may appear only as provider-owned reference identities in positively declared application policy.
guarantees: Secret values never enter operation catalogs, bundles, locks, catalog projections, command arguments, diagnostics, or evidence.
exclusions: No credential acquisition design, query-string secret, secret persistence, or guessed redaction.

persistence.policy: Persist exact content-addressed source bytes, separate tool and capability locks, owned provider entries/wrappers, and one derived flat catalog.
guarantees: Derived projections are deterministic and atomically replaced.
Manual projection edits are detectable drift and never authoritative.
Refresh uses unchanged verified source and a valid lock; update alone accepts changed source.
exclusions: No original-source re-resolution after acquisition, lock adoption after tamper, unrelated provider-file mutation, or runtime-owned AI workspace edit.

failure.policy: Fail closed with stable classifications when identity, schema, closure, compatibility, provider, ownership, proposal, or byte evidence is absent or changed.
guarantees: Tool-ready and agent-guided failures remain independent and identify exact blockers.
Incomplete knowledge closure blocks before guided execution.
Application diagnostics, bridge execution failures, protocol failures, and Program Kit conformance failures remain distinct.
exclusions: No silent omission, guessed remediation, fallback source, retry, partial mutation, inferred success, or Program Kit application-result envelope.

concurrency.policy: Operation concurrency is exact application-owned policy and lifecycle mutation uses atomic one-bundle/provider ownership.
guarantees: The bridge enforces selected operation limits and starts one bounded consumer execution per accepted call.
Catalog projection is deterministic under a serialized accepted mutation.
exclusions: No unbounded queue, shared application process, implicit parallelism, concurrent lock adoption, or automatic retry.

cancellation.policy: Advertise and translate cancellation only when exact operation and adapter contracts support it; enforce bounded timeout separately.
guarantees: Cancellation races and timeouts have explicit evidence classifications.
Capability procedure stop conditions remain guidance and do not alter executable cancellation contracts.
exclusions: No rollback, idempotency, or side-effect reversal claim from cancellation or timeout.

observability.policy: Record exact identities, versions, digests, proposal/lock transitions, provider versions, trust/permission observations, readiness, process boundaries, and canonical result digests without secret or reasoning content.
guarantees: Publisher-official and Program Kit-conformant claims remain separate.
Provider-neutral and provider-labelled evidence remain separate.
Genuine provider closure stays open when exact cold-session evidence is absent.
exclusions: No provider reasoning equivalence, prompt equivalence, raw secret/input/result capture, inferred trust, or fabricated external evidence.

compatibility.policy: Pin exact semantic versions and digests and require reviewed explicit transitions for every operation, tool, bundle, provider, or projection change.
guarantees: Modern 2026-07-28 and legacy 2025-11-25 MCP profiles are explicit.
Compatible additions never silently enter an existing registration or initialized capability set.
Provider contract drift blocks the affected transition.
exclusions: No latest selector, floating version, inferred cross-host equivalence, auto-upgrade, silent refresh-to-new-source, or unreviewed migration.
